intended_object: The map given by the universal property of the zigzag quotient kQ̄/I, where I is the two-sided ideal generated by the zigzag relators. A k-algebra map f out of the path algebra of the doubled quiver that kills every relator induces a unique k-algebra map out of the quotient. Inferred from the docstring and from how `nonisolatedZigzagQuotient` is defined.
explanation:
`nonisolatedZigzagQuotient k G` is, by definition, `pathAlgebra k (DoubledQuiver G) ⧸ (zigzagIdeal k G).asIdeal`. Here `zigzagIdeal` is `TwoSidedIdeal.span {x | IsZigzagRelator k G x}`.

If f kills every generator, the earlier lemma `zigzagIdeal_le_ker` shows that the span lies in the kernel of f. The definition then applies Mathlib's `Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ` to get the induced map, so it is exactly the universal-property map. Its hypotheses are the right ones: an arbitrary target k-algebra B, and f vanishing on the generating relators.

It specialises Mathlib's general quotient lift to one particular quotient. It is a convenience wrapper for a specific object (the companion lemma `zigzagLift_zigzagMk` confirms that it agrees with f on classes), not a general notion written out in a narrow setting. So it is faithful.
